Do you have a definition of Open Data reuse in your country?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please specify it.
column4: Definition of Open Data re-use is specifed in the Law of Ukraine on Access to Public Information https://zakon.rada.gov.ua/laws/show/2939-17#n259 in the very definition of Open Data: "Public information in the form of Open Data is public information in a format that allows its automated electronic processing, free and free access to it, and its further re-use. Dataproviders are obliged to provide public information in the form of Open Data on request, publish and regularly update it on the national portal and on their websites. Public information in the form of Open Data is allowed for its further free re-use and dissemination. Any person is free to copy, publish, distribute, re-use, including for commercial purposes, in combination with other information or by including in their own product, public information in the form of Open Data with mandatory reference to the source of such information .

column2:
Do you have a methodology in place to measure the impact of Open Data in your country?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe the key points of this methodology.
column4: The Ministry of Digital Transformation employ a framework to measure the impact of Open Data. We have utilized international best practices such as NYU’s GovLab project https://odimpact.org/ . Qualitative approach to its Open Data impact measurement is used . Typical Open Data impact research involves pre-screening of potential subjects either from a bottom-up approach (a large number of Open Data products found in a specific domain or from a specific Open Dataset) or a top-down one (research into a specific governmental body or domain, e.g. ecology, state regulatory commission, health, etc). The research relies heavily on interviews and focus-groups with parties involved in opening the data (state officials, data scientists), creating and using products based on these data (NGOs, civil activists, journalists, etc). The impact is measured by analysis of several key categories, namely: does it help prevent or detect corruption; does it provide new tools for civil impact; how many users of the Open Data and tools created on the basis of the Open Data? and does it improve social standards? Interviews with the before-mentioned parties allow to gain as much of an objective view of Open Data impact as possible.

column7:
In order to increase the transparency of state institutions to solve socio-economic problems and to support innovative projects, grant competitions for startups are organized based on Open Data.
In June 2023, the competition "Open Data. Unbroken" together with OSCE was organized. https://www.openunbroken.org/. Winners: "Where's the shelter?" — a chatbot for finding the nearest bomb shelter in Ukraine. https://shelteruabot.com/. "VPO Nazar" is a chatbot to help internally displaced persons integrate into a new environment https://citybot.pro/vpo. "Plant Varieties" is an information aggregator that brings together resources such as Plant Varieties and Controlled Pesticides https://agrarii-razom.com.ua/. 
Also in November 2023 the competition "Open Datathon reUkraine" together with TAPAS project was organized https://datathon.data.gov.ua/. Among the winners of the competition is the service for providing access to public registers for citizens and businesses "Opendatabot" https://opendatabot.ua/, the solution for finding barrier-free locations "Dostupno!" from the Ukrainian Center for Social Data https://dostupno.ua/mapa-dostupnosti/, chatbot "I'll be a mother" from the "Liky Kontrol" team https://chats.viber.com/iwillbemother_bot, a system of dashboards with analytics from the Clarity Project — Clarity Hromada https://clarity-project.info/hromada.
In addition "Open Data Hackathon" with support of DTA project is running now. More than 230 applications for participation received. https://www.opendatatech.org/hackathon. 
In addition, increasing the level of competence in the field of Open Data is one of the priority directions of the Open Data community in Ukraine.
With the support of international partners, a course on Open Data was prepared for journalism students and other humanities majors. Currently, this course is being implemented in the educational system of certain institutions of higher education.
This will ensure the sustainability of Open Data (a ready-made audience of interested youth), which will attract new users of Open Data, encourage data providers to publish more information in the form of Open Data, and replenish the labor market with specialists who know how to use Open Data.
In the future, the program will be implemented in other higher education institutions and in other specialties.

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide a brief explanation of the process: How does the gathering happen?
column4:
In Ukraine, the basis for confirming the case of reuse of a data set is a software product (application) that uses data sets in its work.  Ministry of Digital Transformation maintains a complete list of all applications/visualizations/dashboards and analytical panels in a special section of the Open Data Competence Center Diia.Open Data.
The developers themselves submit their product for publication, it is necessary to specify the datasets used in the product. After the inspection,  Ministry either approves and publishes such a product, or returns the application to the developer for revision.

column4: Monitoring of the exercise of powers by deputies of local self-government. According to the latest study Social and anti-corruption impact of Open Data on local comunities (part 2) https://tapas.org.ua/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/OD_municipalities_part-2.pdf residents' understanding of the duties of deputies of local councils creates more opportunities for solving community problems, as there is no room for manipulation, instead there is a field for discussions and cooperation. Dataset "Data on deputies of local councils, including contact details and reception schedule" allows citizens to find out the following information: biographical data, phone number, e-mail address, pages in social networks, faction name and position in it, standing committee name and position in it, etc. Disclosure of data about MPs with reception schedule and contact information, as well as the results of MP activity can significantly simplify the processes of activity monitoring and feedback. Information collected in one place and presented in a convenient form increases the accountability of representatives in power to their constituents. "Analytics of deputy activity" is a service that provides the publication of projects, adopted decisions, the course of voting and analytics of the work of council deputies. Hosted on the Drohobych Smart City platform, it was launched on May 14, 2021. The system contains a created profile of each deputy with detailed information on voting statistics, proposed projects and amendments, and affiliation to factions. This helps the residents to be aware of the votes and not to allow the deputies to mislead the residents about the projects implemented in the city.

With the help of interactive services and products created on the basis of Open Data in the medical field, citizens receive information on signing declarations with physicians in a clear and informative format.
Creating services based on Open Data helps attract citizens and pharmacies to the Affordable Medicine program, providing the following information in an accessible and efficient format: to patients about the availability of medicines that can be received on a free-of-charge basis, to pharmacy owners about the location of participating pharmacies,
the level of competition in the market and the amount of payments to pharmacies and, accordingly, the analysis of opportunities to participate in the program. Big Recovery Portal receives data from the public ARI DREAM, and for each project applies a risk analysis based on a set of criteria developed by itself (cost estimate, financing, type and duration of recovery, availability of tender documentation, availability of reporting). column2: 4.3d Economic impact

Is any data on the economic impact (e.g. GDP, employment, productivity, innovation,  new businesses created etc.) of Open Data available in your country such as from research studies, impact assessments, or other systematic investigations that quantify the results or broader effects of Open Data being reused?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please specify what kind of data source proves this impact and provide the URLs to this data.
column4:
In Ukraine, the economic effect of Open Data is divided into direct and secondary. Direct economic impacts include the economic value created by enterprises that provide services using Open Data, as well as the corresponding employment. Employment is considered to have a direct economic impact if the organization bases its business or activities on Open Data (for example, a startup that would not be able to operate without Open Data, or a civil servant working with a national portal).The creation of economic value in the macroeconomic sense involves the creation of gross value added. The latter includes three components: gross profit of the enterprise, wages of employees and taxes paid on products and taxes related to production (excluding subsidies). In other words, the business generates certain profits for its investors, employees and the state. Open data companies, like any business, also create gross value added - it is a direct economic contribution of such companies. https://kse.ua/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Open-data-methodology-2021-11-04.pdf

Responce to reviewer:
Report on Economic Impact of Open Data in Ukraine has been developed (https://tapas.org.ua/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Economic-impact_report.pdf).
The report analyzed three key indicators: 1) the impact of Open Data on the Ukrainian economy; 2) the number of jobs related to Open Data in the country; and 3) the sectors of the Ukrainian economy that benefit the most from Open Data. 
The information presented in the report is based on the pace of economic development and advancement in the Ukrainian Open Data sphere until Russia invaded Ukraine on February 24, 2022. 
One of its findings was that Open Data contributed between 0.62-1.19% of Ukraine’s gross domestic product (GDP) in 2020. 
The Open Data sphere could contribute between 0.78-2.08% to Ukraine’s economy i.e., UAH 49.9 billion ($167 million) by 2025 through a combination of direct and indirect benefits. 
The research also found that the number of Ukrainians working directly with Open Data is between 4,400 - 6,700. In 2025, somewhere between 23,600 to 50,800 people could be working with Open Data. 
Top sectors working with Open Data in Ukraine include: IT and telecommunications; scientific and technical activities; public administration; real estate, transportation; and postal and courier services. This was TAPAS’ second study on the impact of Open Data on Ukraine’s economy.

Open data has an impact on the level on employment. Today more than 100 available open data services help Ukrainians to check business partners, receive free medicines and medical services, safely invest in real estate, etc. Such services create new jobs for citizens of Ukraine (source: https://tapas.org.ua/all-uk/news-uk/mintsyfra-prezentuvala-viziiu-rozvytku-vidkrytykh-danykh-v-ukraini/). The total employment in the field of open data in 2020 was 15.9-24.5 thousand people. According to the State Statistics Service, in 2020 there were about 7.5 million full-time workers in Ukraine. Since Ukraine is part of the cluster of "fast developing countries", the share of direct employment related to open data is about 0.09% of all employees. Accordingly, under the implementation of the optimistic scenario, direct employment in the field of open data amounts to 6.7 thousand people. If employment grew in accordance with the growth of the general open data market, then under a conservative scenario, direct employment amounts to 4,400 people. However, in addition to direct employment, open data also provides indirect employment. According to research by Shakespeare and Vickery, the indirect open data market is 250-278% of the direct market. Taking into account the average value of these studies, indirect employment related to open data is 11.5-7.8 thousand people (according to research https://tapas.org.ua/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Economic-impact_report.pdf)

Experts from the R&D center at YouControl analyzed the influence of women on various sectors of Ukrainian business during the wartime year. They found that women significantly contributed by continuing the activities of existing companies and opening new ones. https://blog.youcontrol.market/iak-ukrayinki-pidtrimuiut-biznies-sieriedovishchie/ 
YouControl conducted research for 2023 to ascertain the professional fields and industries that women entrepreneurs gravitate toward. The study yielded findings that indicate large-scale enterprises remain a predominantly male-dominated domain. The research revealed that among the top 1,000 corporations ranked by revenue generation in 2023, a mere 7% were under the corporate ownership of women entrepreneurs, while an additional 11% operated under a mixed ownership structure involving both male and female proprietors. https://blog.youcontrol.market/zhinochie-oblichchia-bizniesu-iaki-sfieri-obiraiut-zhinki-ta-chomu-vielikii-biznies-dosi-zalishaietsia-cholovichim/ 
OpenDatabot has released the Index of the Premier Enterprises of Ukraine for the year 2024. This comprehensive index is compiled utilizing data sourced from state registries, corporate financial statements, sanctioned entities lists, and other analytical resources. It offers in-depth insights into sales performance categorized by industry sector and geographic region. The information presented in this index can serve as a tool for private entrepreneurs to strategically plan their business by identifying sectors and locations where their enterprises may achieve greater profitability.
https://opendatabot.ua/analytics/opendatabot-index-2024.
Based on Open Data, the Opendatabot project systematically analyzes the activities of private entrepreneurs, including gender distribution. According to the latest research, 59% of new private enterprises in Ukraine in 2024 were opened by women.
Women entrepreneurs most often choose the following activities:
Retail trade (68% women and 32% men);
Provision of other individual services (89% women and 11% men);
Provision of information services (63% women and 37% men)
